A low intensity threshold of 4 kW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is observed, with a contrast of 65% between the high and low reflectivity states.

articleTitle: Maximizing on-axis coupling efficiency between single mode fiber and multimode specialty fibers using multi-mode interference
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Novel technique to optimize on-axis coupling between single mode fiber and multimode specialty fibers using an intermediate segment of step index multimode fiber is presented. Coupling efficiency of 93% is achieved for optimum fiber parameters.

articleTitle: Thermal lensing in oxide-confined, single-mode VCSELs
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: High spatial and thermal resolution measurements of the surface temperature of an operating single-mode oxide-confined VCSEL are reported. We show that the beam waist scales with the focal length of the thermal lens.

Index Terms: Singlemode Vertical Cavity Surface Emitting Lasers

articleTitle: Slow light in nonlinear fibre Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We demonstrate slow light by exciting gap solitons in a 10 cm apodized fibre Bragg grating. Propagation at 0.23 c/n with little pulse distortion, corresponding to a delay of over 1.6 ns, is observed.

articleTitle: Phase-matched third-order frequency generation in TiO2 rutile single crystal
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We investigated third harmonic generation and triple photon generation properties of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> rutile single crystal, including phase-matching and figure of merit. We demonstrated that TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is more efficient than KTiOPO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>.

articleTitle: The refractive index of dye/polymer composite films
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Designing photonic devices using organic nonlinear dye/polymer composites requires an accurate determination of the index. A model of the wavelength and concentration dependence of the index that includes the density dependence is given.

articleTitle: Lattice surface solitons
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: It is theoretically shown that nonlinear surface-waves are possible in optical lattices. Such solitons can exist at the interface between two different semi-infinite 1D waveguide arrays and also at the boundaries of a 2D lattice.

articleTitle: Ultrashort-pulse light-assisted periodic poling of lithium niobate and lithium tantalate
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: We report the light-assisted poling of controllable periodic and arbitrarily-shaped domain patterns in lithium niobate and lithium tantalate via the simultaneous application of a low uniform DC electric-field and sequence of ultrashort pulses (150-200 fs).

articleTitle: Characterization of UV-induced benzocyclobutene optical waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics and 2006 Quantum Electronics and Laser Science Conference
abstract: Singl e-mode non-ridge benzocyclobutene optical waveguides fabricated by excimer laser illumination are presented. The induced index change is about 0.003 after 50 shot s of laser pulse exposure. The propagation loss at 1548nm is about 0.6dB/cm.
